'''Eva Konrad Hawkins''' (March 12, 1930 – April 18, 2020) was a Hungarian-born American biologist and college professor.

== Early life ==
Éva Konrád was raised in [[Berettyóújfalu]], near [[Debrecen|Debrecen, Hungary]], to Jewish parents József Konrád and Róza Klein. Her younger brother was writer [[György Konrád]]. The siblings lived in a safe house in Budapest during [[World War II]]; their parents survived the [[Strasshof an der Nordbahn|Strasshof]] [[Nazi concentration camps|concentration camp]] in Austria.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Schwartz|first=Penny|date=2020-06-18|title=Eva Konrad Hawkins, 90, Holocaust survivor who designed underwater museum exhibits|url=https://www.jta.org/2020/06/18/bonds-of-life/eva-konrad-hawkins-90-holocaust-survivor-who-designed-underwater-museum-exhibits|access-date=2020-12-05|website=Jewish Telegraphic Agency|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|agency=Associated Press|date=2019-09-14|title=Gyorgy Konrad, Writer and Dissident in Communist Hungary, Dies at 86 (Published 2019)|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2019/09/14/obituaries/gyorgy-konrad-writer-dissident-dead.html|access-date=2020-12-05|issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

Konrád moved to the United States after the [[Hungarian Revolution of 1956]], after walking to Austria in snow, with a backpack of her belongings. In 1961, she completed doctoral studies in botany at the [[University of Pennsylvania]],<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|last=Kilgannon|first=Corey|date=2020-06-11|title=Eva Konrad Hawkins, Marine Scientist Who Fled Hungary, Dies at 90|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/06/11/obituaries/eva-konrad-hawkins-dead-coronavirus.html|access-date=2020-12-05|issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-08-20|title=Obituaries|url=https://thepenngazette.com/obituaries-47/|access-date=2020-12-05|website=The Pennsylvania Gazette|language=en-US}}</ref> with a dissertation on the [[Callithamnion roseum]], a type of red seaweed.<ref>Konrad, Eva. "Developmental Studies on Regenerates of Callithamnion roseum, Harvey" (PhD. dissertation, University of Pennsylvania, 1961).</ref>

== Career ==
Hawkins taught biology at the University of Pennsylvania, the [[University of Delaware]],<ref>{{Cite book|last=University of Delaware|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=6oAI6rJe-yoC&q=Eva+Konrad+Hawkins|title=Graduate Catalog|date=1963|pages=130|language=en}}</ref> [[Fairleigh Dickinson University]], and [[City College of New York]].<ref name=":0" /> She was an [[algae]] expert on the staff of the [[Wildlife Conservation Society|New York Zoological Society]]'s Osborn Laboratory of Marine Sciences, supported by a [[Rockefeller Foundation]] grant.<ref>{{Cite book|last=New York Zoological Society|url=http://archive.org/details/annualreportofne7219newy|title=Annual report of the New York Zoological Society|date=1967|pages=61|publisher=New York Zoological Society |via=Internet Archive}}</ref> She designed underwater exhibits for the [[American Museum of Natural History]] and the [[New York Aquarium]]. She held a research fellowship at the [[New York Botanical Garden]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=New York Botanical Garden|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=aLvkAAAAMAAJ&q=Eva+Konrad+Hawkins|title=The New York Botanical Garden Newsletter|date=1967|pages=5|language=en}}</ref>

Hawkins's research was published in scholarly journals including ''[[American Journal of Botany]]'',<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Hawkins|first=Eva Konrad|title=Induction of Cell Differentiation in Dissociated Cells and Fragments of Callithamnion Roseum|date=February 1968|url=http://doi.wiley.com/10.1002/j.1537-2197.1968.tb06969.x|journal=American Journal of Botany|language=en|volume=55|issue=2|pages=255–264|doi=10.1002/j.1537-2197.1968.tb06969.x|bibcode=1968AmJB...55..255H |url-access=subscription}}</ref> ''[[Journal of Cell Science]],''<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Hawkins|first=Eva Konrad|date=1974-05-01|title=Growth and Differentiation of the Golgi Apparatus in the Red Alga, Callithamnion Roseum|url=https://jcs.biologists.org/content/14/3/633|journal=Journal of Cell Science|language=en|volume=14|issue=3|pages=633–655|doi=10.1242/jcs.14.3.633|issn=0021-9533|pmid=4830835|doi-access=free|url-access=subscription}}</ref> ''[[International Phycological Society|Phycologia]],''<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Hawkins|first=Eva Konrad|date=1972-03-01|title=Cell differentiation in tetrasporophytes of Callithamnion roseum Harvey (Rhodophyceae, Ceramiales)|url=https://doi.org/10.2216/i0031-8884-11-1-37.1|journal=Phycologia|volume=11|issue=1|pages=37–41|doi=10.2216/i0031-8884-11-1-37.1|bibcode=1972Phyco..11...37H |issn=0031-8884|url-access=subscription}}</ref> [[American Microscopical Society|''Transactions of the American Microscopical Society'']],<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hawkins|first1=Eva Konrad|last2=Lee|first2=John J.|date=1990|title=Fine Structure of the Cell Surface of a Cultured Endosymbiont Strain of Porphyridium sp. (Rhodophyta)|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/3226689|journal=Transactions of the American Microscopical Society|volume=109|issue=4|pages=352–360|doi=10.2307/3226689|jstor=3226689|issn=0003-0023|url-access=subscription}}</ref> ''[[Curator: The Museum Journal]]'',<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Hawkins|first=Eva K.|date=March 1970|title=Ecological and Visual Considerations in Creating a Diorama of a Submarine Environment|url=http://doi.wiley.com/10.1111/j.2151-6952.1970.tb00395.x|journal=Curator: The Museum Journal|language=en|volume=13|issue=1|pages=69–88|doi=10.1111/j.2151-6952.1970.tb00395.x|url-access=subscription}}</ref> ''[[Journal of Phycology]]'',<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hawkins|first1=Eva K.|last2=Lee|first2=John J.|last3=Fimiarz|first3=Daniel K.|date=2011|title=Colony Formation and Sexual Morphogenesis in the Coccolithophore Pleurochrysis Sp. (haptophyta)1|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/j.1529-8817.2011.01044.x|journal=Journal of Phycology|language=en|volume=47|issue=6|pages=1344–1349|doi=10.1111/j.1529-8817.2011.01044.x|pmid=27020358|bibcode=2011JPcgy..47.1344H |s2cid=38628560|issn=1529-8817|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and ''Protoplasma''.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Hawkins|first=Eva Konrad|date=1974-03-01|title=Golgi vesicles of uncommon morphology and wall formation in the red alga, Polysiphonia|url=https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01666347|journal=Protoplasma|language=en|volume=80|issue=1|pages=1–14|doi=10.1007/BF01666347|pmid=4833207|bibcode=1974Prpls..80....1H |s2cid=34289363|issn=1615-6102|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Eva Konrád married Charles Hawkins in the 1960s. They later divorced. She became a naturalized United States citizen in 1963.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Spruance|first=John S.|date=1963-09-13|title=Polish Scientist Who Got Asylum Among 74 on Naturalization List|pages=25|work=The News Journal|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/64653571/polish-scientist-who-got-asylum-among/|access-date=2020-12-05|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> She died from [[COVID-19]] at a nursing home in the [[The Bronx|Bronx]] on April 18, 2020, aged 90.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-07-03|title=In memory of 5 more U.S. victims of the coronavirus|url=https://www.pbs.org/newshour/show/in-memory-of-5-more-u-s-victims-of-the-coronavirus|access-date=2020-12-05|website=PBS NewsHour|language=en-us}}</ref>
